clauses.reason: Paragraph 1 closes the departments and agencies in the District of Columbia "all day on Tuesday, December 24,1940" and excuses employees from duty "on that day." The command therefore covers one calendar day and ended with that day by its own terms. The end is recorded as December 24, 1940, inclusive; the exclusive reading, under which it ends when that day begins, is the alternative. No held instrument revokes, extends or amends it, and the exceptions in the paragraph do not extend its period.

Paragraph 2 directs that the order be published in the Federal Register. It is a one-time direction that was performed when the order appeared in the Federal Register issue dated Wednesday, December 18, 1940, as the masthead of the held page shows; the filing line in the held text gives the earlier date December 17, 1940, which is an alternative reading. After publication the paragraph has no further subject. No held instrument revokes, extends or amends it.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 8613 of December 16, 1940 (5 FR 5143, Federal Register issue of Wednesday, December 18, 1940; FR Doc. 40-5680, filed December 17, 1940) closes the executive departments and other agencies in the District of Columbia, and excuses Federal employees from duty, for the single day Tuesday, December 24, 1940, with exceptions for employees excluded by agency heads for special public reasons or whose absence would be inconsistent with existing law (paragraph 1), and directs that the order be published in the Federal Register (paragraph 2). Both paragraphs were spent by their own terms. Paragraph 2 was performed when the order appeared in the issue dated December 18, 1940; the filing line gives the earlier date December 17, 1940, which is an alternative reading. Paragraph 1 applied to one calendar day and had no subject afterwards. Following the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on stated dates, the end of paragraph 1 is recorded as December 24, 1940, inclusive (the order runs through that day); the exclusive reading, under which it ends when December 24 begins, is the alternative. The working text is the official Federal Register page text extracted from the PDF by OCR, not an authenticated transcription; page images were not inspected.

savings.reason: The closure and the excusal from duty on December 24, 1940 took effect on that day and accrued to the employees concerned. That result is a past consequence of the executed order, not a command that Executive Order 8613 continues to impose. The held text has no savings clause, and no held source shows any right or duty extending beyond that day.
